newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end narrowly mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end narrowly mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Shares on Lima stock exchange closed broadly stable Monday as investors generally remained on the sidelines in an absence of economic news, brokers said.
They added Tuesday's trade was expected to show the same trend.
Monday, the General Index .IGRA edged down 0.12 percent to 1,435.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index nudged up 0.01 percent to 1,976.1 points, according to preliminary stock figures.

While trade was sluggish on the whole, two large cross-trades -- or transactions within the same brokerage -- in benchmark Telefonica del Peru lifted volume to 48.5 million soles ($19.5 million), brokers said.
Telefonica closed down 0.69 percent at 5.73 soles on volume of 4.49 million shares.
Foreign investors were noticeably absent from the market and believed to be concentrating their funds on U.S. equity markets, brokers said.
Local investors were also cautious, however, as the resignation of Presidency Minister Jaime Yoshiyama at the weekend had provoked some uncertainty about the government's stability, they added.
"While (the resignation) did not have a serious negative effect, it was enough to keep some players on the sidelines," said Alex Valerin of local brokerage Macrovalores.
The replacement for Yoshiyama, who resigned from one of the government's top posts for personal reasons, is expected to be announced later Monday.

Among leaders, the brewery sector saw the most activity with Backus y Johnston closing unchanged at 2.50 soles on 932,000 shares. Cervesur closed up 2.5 percent on 290,000 shares and Compania Nacional de Cerveza fell 1.1 percent to 0.90 soles on 264,000 shres
Also, polymetallic miner Atacocha closed unchanged at 0.33 soles on 286,000 shares.
In a total of 1,736 operations, 32 stocks rose, 25 fell and 32 were stable.
